title: Cobalt Health - On-prem / Air-gapped Discovery
summary: Discovery call to evaluate Redwood private on-prem / air-gapped deployment for a regulated health provider. Key concerns: air-gapped update process, hardware/GPUs available, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, SOC2/ISO evidence, timeline and success criteria for POC. AE+SE from Redwood will send pricing, security pack, and propose a short pilot with offline image delivery and benchmark plan.
next_steps: Redwood to share security pack (SOC2, ISO docs) and on-prem deployment guide by 2026-04-02
Redwood SE to propose POC benchmark plan and hardware checklist by 2026-04-05
Cobalt to share list of on-prem hardware specs and compliance constraints by 2026-04-01
Schedule POC kickoff (2-week window) week of 2026-04-12
action_items: Samir Gupta (Redwood) - Draft POC benchmark plan and offline image delivery steps; due 2026-04-05
Jamie Patel (Redwood) - Send pricing and Dedicated vs Private comparison deck + security pack; due 2026-04-02
Priya Singh (Cobalt) - Share hardware inventory (GPU types, network isolation details) and list of stakeholders for compliance review; due 2026-04-01
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-29 16:00 PDT; Duration: ~46 minutes; Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Marquez (CTO), Mark Reynolds (Head of Infra), Priya Singh (Security)

[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Jamie from Redwood, i'm the account lead, with me is Samir our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Elena: good thanks, jen -- uh Elena here. thanks for the time. we wanted to go through how an on-prem, air gapped deployment would look for our environment and what the constraints are.
[00:22] Mark: yeah, hi all. quick note we are fully isolated for PHI workloads, so no egress, and updates have to be pushed via offline media.
[00:30] Samir: great, thanks. just to level set, we support three deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private which can be VPC or fully on-prem air-gapped. sounds like you're looking at Private, specifically air-gapped?
[00:41] Priya: correct. our compliance team won't let PHI leave the network. we also have H S M-backed KMS and strict key rotation.
[00:51] Jamie: totally understood. can you walk us through your hardware and patch/update cadence?
[00:56] Mark: sure. currently we have a small GPU cluster: two racks with A40s and one older A100 node, but the network is restricted and there's no direct internet. Updates are monthly but must be staged and approved.
[01:12] Samir: okay, A40s and A100, noted. performance profiles change a lot on different cards; we'll capture that in the benchmark plan. is there an existing air-gap process for other packages? like offline install media or air-gapped docker registries?
[01:26] Elena: yes, we use an internal artifact repo that gets mirrored via physical media by Ops. tends to be a manual process.
[01:33] Samir: perfect, that's workable. our on-prem package supports offline image import — we provide signed artifacts and a verification step so you can validate checksum and signatures. you mentioned H S M, do you have a KMS vendor?
[01:45] Priya: we're on Thales for H S M and use internal KMS for keys; we require FIPS 140-2 certs and integration for model encryption at rest.
[01:55] Jamie: we can support KMS integrations; typically for private deployments we integrate with customer KMS via an H S M bridge or use local key wrapping. we'll include the exact integration patterns in the security pack.
[02:06] Mark: what about offline updates for model weights and runtime? we can't pull from cloud.
[02:11] Samir: two patterns: 1) offline artifact delivery — we hand you a signed tarball with model weights + runtime container images; you import into your registry and verify signatures. 2) air-gapped appliance — we can ship a sealed appliance image that your infra loads. both require a controlled process for checksum verification and a short restart window.
[02:31] Elena: how do you handle KV cache and tokenization consistency across restarts? we need to ensure identical behavior for evals.
[02:39] Samir: good question, KV cache is persisted optionally — in air-gapped mode we can configure persistent KV store on local storage. tokenization and deterministic seeds are part of the runtime config. there may be slight differences across different GPU types, so we'll run bitwise-comparison tests during the POC.
[02:59] Priya: are there any telemetry or call-home features we need to worry about? our policy forbids telemetry leaving the network.
[03:07] Jamie: default is no telemetry in air-gapped installs. we turn off call-home and can provide local logging only. ops may want log shipping but that's customer controlled.
[03:18] Mark: ok good. can you talk about model updates and vulnerability patches? patching cadence—we'd prefer quarterly runtime updates unless it's a CVE.
[03:28] Samir: we do security patch releases monthly but can bundle into quarterly delivery for you; critical CVE patches we'd push as out-of-band and coordinate via your change control. we'll document the process.
[03:40] Elena: licensing model, how does pricing work for private versus dedicated?
[03:44] Jamie: short version: Hosted is usage-based, Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly commit), Private has an enterprise license plus optional support and deployment fees. for on-prem air-gapped we typically do an annual platform fee plus per-node runtime licenses; i'll send a detailed pricing sheet.
[03:58] Priya: any limitations on model types or quantization? we plan to run a mix of open models and our own fine-tuned variants.
[04:06] Samir: supported model families cover most transformer-based models; quantization paths are supported but depend on GPU and kernel availability. we'll recommend quant profiles per workload. custom models are supported — we assist with model import and conversion.
[04:20] Mark: network constraints — we have strict VLAN segmentation, no external DNS resolution. can the deployment work without external dependency on time servers?
[04:30] Samir: yes, we can run without NTP if you allow a local time service; verification of signatures can be done with local certs. we'll include an ops checklist to walk through required outbound/inbound ports (which in your case will be none).
[04:44] Elena: benchmarks — we'd like to see per-token latency numbers on A40 vs A100 and cost estimates.
[04:51] Samir: we'll do a small benchmark during the POC: 1) baseline throughput/latency with your seq lengths, 2) memory and KV behavior, and 3) perf delta with quantized weights. we'll include CSV outputs so you can plug into your cost model.
[05:06] Mark: are there specific kernel or driver versions we need? our infra team is conservative on driver updates.
[05:12] Samir: minimal driver requirements depend on CUDA and kernel choices; we typically support CUDA 11.8+ for A40 and specific drivers for A100. we can provide a compatibility matrix.
[05:22] Priya: audit logs — we need tamper-evident logs for inference requests and admin actions, retention for 7 years. is that supported?
[05:31] Jamie: yes, our private deployment has audit logging hooks; we can forward to your local SIEM and sign logs for tamper evidence. retention policies are configurable. we'll include archive/export tools in the docs.
[05:44] Elena: any customers in healthcare who've done air-gapped?
[05:47] Jamie: yes, we've worked with a few health and biopharma customers — i can share redacted case studies in the security pack.
[05:55] Mark: how long to get set up for a POC? we have change windows and approvals.
[06:00] Samir: typical POC is 2–4 weeks once we have hardware access and your security approval; initial bench runs can be done in 3–5 days with the right artifacts.
[06:10] Elena: success criteria — what should we measure?
[06:13] Jamie: common criteria: latency SLOs (p95 under X ms), throughput throughput per GPU (reqs/sec), correctness/regression vs your golden prompt set, and operational checklist met (offline updates tested, KMS integration validated).
[06:27] Priya: on governance: we require a third-party code scan, SBOM for all runtime images, and signed bills of materials for model artifacts.
[06:36] Samir: we provide SBOM and signed artifacts; we can run container scans before handoff and include SBOMs with the delivery media.
[06:48] Mark: can you do a sealed appliance approach if we can't run containers?
[06:53] Samir: yes, we can produce an appliance image or provide a hardware-locked bundle; both have tradeoffs on flexibility. we'll document options in the POC plan.
[07:04] Elena: timeline constraints — compliance committee meets monthly, we'd like to align POC to their April review.
[07:10] Jamie: understood — we'll aim to have materials and a proposed kickoff before your committee meeting.

[07:25] -- mid-call quick recap --
[07:25] Jamie: quick recap: Redwood can support air-gapped on-prem with offline artifact delivery, H S M/KMS integration, telemetry off, audit logs local, and we will provide a POC benchmark plan. deliverables: security pack, pricing, POC plan, hardware checklist.
[07:43] Priya: that matches our asks. a few clarifying points on offline updates — do you sign model weights with customer keys or Redwood keys?
[07:52] Samir: we support both. we can sign with Redwood for chain-of-custody and provide tooling so you re-sign with your keys on import. for highest assurance you can re-sign locally.
[08:04] Mark: what about image verification tooling?
[08:07] Samir: we'll hand over a verification script and checksums; the process mirrors your internal artifact import.
[08:13] Elena: ok, let's talk about the POC scope — we want a small pilot with 2 model variants, one open LLM and one fine-tuned clinical model, run inference on a subset of prompts and check for regressions.
[08:25] Samir: sounds good. we'll propose sample prompts, measurement scripts, and expected outputs. will you be able to provide a golden prompt set?
[08:33] Elena: yes, security will vet it, but we can share an initial set by next week.
[08:38] Jamie: perfect. any blockers on our side getting approvals?
[08:42] Priya: main blocker is security review of SBOM and third-party libs. once we see those, we can clear a small pilot.
[08:50] Jamie: we'll prioritize sending SBOM and security artifacts.
[08:53] Mark: small note, our ops team wants a maintenance window for any restarts during the POC — we'll provide windows.
[08:59] Samir: understood — we'll coordinate with your ops calendar.
[09:04] Priya: backup / DR — what is the recommended backup approach for model weights and KV caches?
[09:10] Samir: we recommend encrypted backups to local object storage and optionally tape for long retention. we'll include restore test steps.
[09:18] Elena: sounds good. last question: does Redwood do any assisted on-site install for the first deploy?
[09:24] Jamie: we offer an assisted install as an add-on; typically remote install works for most customers but on-site is available for air-gapped if needed.
[09:33] Elena: ok. thanks — we have enough to move to the next step.
[09:37] Jamie: great. we'll send the items we discussed. thanks everyone.
[09:42] Priya: thanks.
[09:44] Mark: thanks.

Notes: transcript contains occasional stutters and mislabeled acronyms; timestamps approximate. References: shared deck (https://redwood.ai/deck/cobalt-po), security pack link: https://redwood.ai/security-pack/cobalt.

End of transcript.
